# Benchmark corpus

Frozen Experiment Planner outputs, one file per case, replayed by
`research-pipeline coder-benchmark run` to give the Coder Agent a number that
can be compared across changes. See `../benchmark.py` for what is scored and
why `interpretable` is the metric to read first.

**These files are hand-written and must not be regenerated by a model.** The
whole value of a held-out set is that it does not move under you: if the corpus
changes between two runs, the comparison measures the corpus rather than the
change, and `compare` will say so by reporting cases present on only one side.

## Adding a case

1. Copy the nearest existing file and give the plan a **globally unique**
   `hypothesis_id` (`H1NN` — cases are matched across runs by that id, so a
   duplicate silently collapses two cases into one).
2. Name the file `NN_short_description.json`; the stem becomes the run
   directory and the label in reports.
3. Keep it to a single plan. Each case runs in its own experiments/output
   directory precisely so per-run state — `CODER_MAX_SLURM_JOBS_PER_RUN`, the
   shared-infrastructure build — cannot make one case's outcome depend on which
   cases ran before it.
4. `uv run pytest tests/test_coder_benchmark.py` checks it against the
   Experiment Planner's own output contract, which is what the Coder Agent
   validates its input against.

Add a case when a real run exposes a route the corpus does not cover — that is
what the coverage test guards. Do not add cases to make a number look better.

## What the current twelve cover

| Case | Exercises |
|---|---|
| 01 tabular classification | the `classification` starter, synthetic data, low complexity |
| 02 regression real download | an openly downloadable source, medium complexity |
| 03 text classification | the `text_classification` starter and the Hub dataset lookup |
| 04 clustering | the `clustering` starter |
| 05 timeseries forecast | no starter match — the "general", example-free prompt |
| 06 deep learning GPU | `needs_gpu` with no GPU present: the sbatch deferral |
| 07 high complexity CPU | `high` complexity deferral without a GPU requirement |
| 08 infeasible scale | `feasible: false` — the skipped path |
| 09 restricted clinical data | a restricted source, so the provenance gate withholds the verdict |
| 10 Monte Carlo simulation | precision cost knobs (`draws`, `chains`) that downscaling may shrink |
| 11 bootstrap resampling | resampling knobs, low complexity |
| 12 embedding benchmark | a plan declaring shared infrastructure |
